24: Adjusted spell bonus = spell bonus × class Magic coefficient; round to the nearest whole number, with exactly 0.5 rounded up.
25: MATK = INT + adjusted spell bonus + LB + sum of applicable item +MATK bonuses.
27: MDEF = INT + LB + magical protection bonus.
29: Magical damage = MAGICAL ATTACK − MAGICAL DEFENCE; a result of 0 or less means 0 damage.
31: The Magic coefficient applies only to a spell's numerical MATK bonus, and the Healing coefficient only to a spell's base healing. Both results are rounded to the nearest whole number, with exactly 0.5 rounded up. Additional equipment bonuses are not multiplied by these coefficients.
33: Spell knowledge: Meeting Min. INT and any Min. Level only allows a character to learn a spell. The character may cast it only after actually acquiring it.
34: Min. INT and equipment: Learning uses the character's permanent INT, excluding item and temporary bonuses. Once properly learned, a spell remains known, and Min. INT is not checked again on each casting. Item INT still increases MATK, MDEF and ordinary INT checks.
35: Acquiring spells: A spell can be acquired when levelling up, from a teacher, book or scroll, as a reward, through discovery or through a story event.
36: Classes: A class does not impose an absolute ban on magic. Characters can learn spells from another school if they meet the requirements and actually acquire them.
37: Min. Level: Min. Level was not subsequently abolished. Ordinary spells use it only where specified; Star Magic always requires high INT, a high Level and knowledge of the specific spell together.
38: Mana: Mana is not used. Powerful spells are limited by requirements, knowledge and a simple usage limit.

97: 5.3 Healing compared with potions and HP – verification calculation
99: Reference comparison: small potion +3 HP, standard +6 HP, large +10 HP. Starting characters have approximately 12–19 HP.
100: Healing (base 4): Healer 4 HP, Ranger 3 HP, Wizard/Bard 2 HP, Warrior/Rogue 1 HP.
101: Healing Light (base 6): Healer 6 HP, matching a standard potion; other classes receive less.
102: Greater Healing (base 10): Healer 10 HP, matching a large potion, but only 1× per adventure.
103: Each caster may use at most 1 spell that applies the Healing coefficient and restores HP per battle. Mass Healing and Regeneration each consume the limit once on casting.
104: The Healer class's First Aid, potions and incidental HP restoration from Drain Life are not healing spells that apply the Healing coefficient, so they do not consume the shared limit.
108: The lowest requirement is INT 14 and Level 12; no starting character meets it.
109: An Elven Wizard starts at INT 10 and can reach INT 14 no earlier than Level 5, if all level-up points up to then go into Intelligence; Min. Level 12 therefore still safely postpones Star Magic.
110: The strongest combat effect is an area bonus of +6, but only 1× per adventure and at INT 16 / Level 16.
111: Spells that change time, resurrection and reality are limited to 1× per adventure or 1× per campaign and require specific knowledge.
112: Ordinary teleportation is not Star Magic; it remains in Air. Open a Gate Between Worlds is a separate ritual for travelling between worlds.
116: The Magic coefficient adjusts only a catalogue spell's bonus, and the Healing coefficient only a spell's base healing. Additional equipment bonuses +MATK, +MDEF, +PDEF and +1 to healing are not multiplied by these coefficients. An attribute bonus first increases the attribute itself.
117: Attack example: a Human Wizard with INT 8, LB 2 and Fire Bolt +2 has MATK 12. A Fire Robe then adds +1 MATK, giving a result of 13. Five active +1 INT items would instead increase INT to 13 and base MATK to 17.

137: A caster maintains at most 1 concentration spell; casting another spell ends it before the new spell is resolved.
138: Starting spells: Wizard 5, Healer 4, Warrior, Ranger, Rogue and Bard 0.
140: A character may learn a spell only if permanent INT, excluding item and temporary bonuses, meets Min. INT, and any Min. Level is met. Meeting the requirements does not itself grant the spell. A properly learned spell remains known, and Min. INT is not checked again on each casting. Min. Level applies; it was not subsequently abolished. Star Magic always requires high permanent INT, a high Level and knowledge of the specific spell.
141: New spells can be acquired when levelling up, from a teacher, book or scroll, as a reward, through discovery or through a story event. Classes and thematic affinity do not impose an absolute ban and add no further numerical bonus in the basic version.
143: General Magic, Fire, Water, Air, Earth, Mind, Spirit, Light Magic, Dark Magic, Nature Magic and Star Magic. Teleportation belongs to Air and Telekinesis to Mind. Star Magic is a mastery school; ordinary teleportation does not belong to it. Dark Magic is not automatically evil.
145: The catalogue of 110 spells serves as a reference for the AI. When a player invents a new spell, Vaelor matches it to the closest reference spell and adopts its approximate INT requirement, Min. Level, bonus, number of targets, duration and restrictions. A new effect must not simultaneously be stronger, affect more targets and have fewer restrictions than its reference.
146: Additional bonuses from all actively equipped items stack without a fixed limit; slots restrict the number of active items. +INT increases MATK and MDEF but does not meet Min. INT for learning. +1 to a magic school means +1 MATK for that school, and +1 to healing means +1 HP to the total result of one casting; both are added after the coefficient. Item PDEF/MDEF bonuses stack with the highest active spell bonus for the relevant defence; multiple spell bonuses to the same PDEF or MDEF do not stack.
